question.note: Asks whether hostile users are more active and have more reach (Expectation 3, p. 2). True, not in the gold.

central_claim.note: A finding, given as a central claim.

flags.text: '2,567 linked users ... about 9.25 million of their public posts' reads as attributing the posts to the 2,567. The paper gives no post count for them.

evidence.note: Lists the survey measures and the Big Five controls. True, not in the gold.

scope_and_limits.note: Says the moderation is suggestive and not causally identified; gold L8 says exploratory outside participation. Credited. JUDGMENT CALL.
Also says the study does not adjudicate between the literatures: the T4 stance, placed under limits.

flags.text: 'They revise the classical treatment of engagement as a single resource construct.' The paper treats its indicators separately (p. 8) but never says the classical literature used a single construct or that it is revising it.

interlocutor_claim.note: Osmundsen et al.: the revisionist view was applied to social media mainly for misinformation sharing; the paper extends it (p. 4). True; kept out of the gold because a model suggested it.
Verba, Schlozman and Brady: engaged citizens have more opportunities to be heard; the paper builds on this for reach (p. 15). True; kept out of the gold because a model suggested it.
The ref. 83 citation rejected as I-x1. Worded as an association, so no distortion: no credit, no flag (labeler agreed).
